meta.name: PLA creep cross-language vectors
meta.description: THE CROSS-LANGUAGE PIN for the sustained-load (creep) allowable. Python (tools/materials.creep_lookup) and Rust (kernel_model::materials::pla::creep_lookup) read the SAME table in tools/materials/pla.json, and this file is the contract they must BOTH satisfy: same allowable, same cell, same refusal, at every tier boundary, on both sides of every boundary, above the hot tier, beyond the last duration column, and for every non-finite / negative input. It exists because the two readers once disagreed above 55 C -- Rust refused (0.0 MPa) while Python returned the 55 C row (1.5 MPa) flagged only by `extrapolated: true`, i.e. the reachable reader was the NON-CONSERVATIVE one. A divergence of that class can now only land by breaking one of the two tests that read this file.
meta.regenerate: This file is a CONTRACT, not a cache. Do not regenerate it to make a failing test pass -- a diff here is a change to a safety semantic and must be argued for. `sig_allow_mpa` 0.0 with a `refusal_kind` means 'no sustained load is defensible', which is an answer, not a gap.

encoding.temp_c/hours: a JSON number, or one of the strings "nan", "inf", "-inf" (JSON has no literal for them)
encoding.across_layer: true applies process.anisotropy.z_vs_xy_strength_ratio (0.55) to the allowable, never to E
encoding.row_used_c/col_used_h: the tabulated cell actually read; null on a refusal
